name: How to Keep Your Deck Looking Great Year-Round

step.name: Step 1
step.text: Keeping your deck in top shape isn't a one-and-done job; it's an ongoing process that pays off in longevity and curb appeal. Think of it as routine care, much like maintaining your car. A good starting point is a thorough annual cleaning and inspection. Some folks even opt for a spring and fall clean-up to stay ahead of things. First, clear off any leaves, dirt, or debris, then give it a good sweep. Next, use an appropriate deck cleaner for your deck's material – wood and composite decks have different needs – and rinse it completely. After cleaning, it’s inspection time. Seriously look at every board, railing, and stair. Check for any signs of rot, splinters, loose fasteners, or warping. For wood decks, resealing every one to two years is often recommended to protect it from the elements. Composite decks generally just need cleaning and inspection, no sealing required. Make sure your drainage is working well to prevent water from pooling, which can lead to premature decay. By catching small issues early, you can often avoid more extensive and costly repairs down the road. If you find anything that looks like it's more than a simple DIY fix, like structural damage or widespread rot, it’s a smart move to call in a pro.
